theme: STR regulation trackers and ordinance datasets: city STR law databases, Legistar/LegiScan clients, EU parliament open data, court records (CourtListener/RECAP) on Airbnb litigation
queries_run: gh search repos "short term rental regulation database" --sort stars
gh search repos "short-term rental ordinance" --sort stars
gh search repos "STR ordinance tracker OR airbnb litigation OR DAC7 platform reporting" --sort stars

candidates.name: js-fitz/STR-Monitor
candidates.what_it_holds: Capstone project on Boston's 2019 STR ordinance enforcement. Committed data: Inside Airbnb Boston scrapes (124,730 listing-rows, 2015-2019, i.e. pre-2023 vintages we do not currently hold), City of Boston STR registration/application records (2,065 matched), Boston Area Research Initiative property assessment parcels (174,074), Padmapper long-term-rental listings (917,948), Street Address Management reference addresses (396,462). Repo has multiple non-empty data directories (Flask App, groupby_neighbs_and_tracts, groupby_prep, mapping) confirmed via GitHub contents API. Method: scraped listings across 23 time periods, Jaro-similarity address matching, built a 'Probability Violation Index' for suspected illegal listings pre/post enforcement (Jan-Dec 2019).
candidates.why_useful: Directly fills gap #1 (historical/archived Inside Airbnb dumps pre-2023 — Boston 2015-2019 vintage we do not hold) and gap #12 (city STR registration/ordinance enforcement dataset). Also touches gap #13 (Padmapper long-term-rental listings for STR/LTR host-supply crossover). A real natural experiment (ordinance date, enforcement date, before/after listing counts) that could anchor an elasticity estimate for regulation impact on supply.
candidates.size_hint: 124,730 listing rows; 917,948 LTR rows; 174,074 parcels; 396,462 addresses

candidates.name: CodeForBc/airbnb-regulation
candidates.what_it_holds: Code for BC civic-tech project building a pipeline to flag Airbnb listings in British Columbia that violate provincial short-term-rental rules: a scraping/data-ingestion module plus a rules-based compliance classifier, output to a Grafana dashboard. No committed regulation text or listing dataset in the repo itself — it is a live scrape+rules method, not a stored dataset.
candidates.why_useful: A working method for detecting non-compliant STR listings against a specific regulatory regime (BC's 2024 provincial STR restrictions); could be adapted as a template for measuring de-facto STR supply compression under new rules elsewhere, but requires running a scraper against Airbnb (a ToS decision, not to be run).

candidates.name: poliquin/pylegiscan
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client wrapping the LegiScan API, which covers bill text, status, votes, and sponsors for all 50 US state legislatures plus Congress. Not STR-specific and holds no committed dataset, but is a working, well-starred (23 stars) way to programmatically pull STR-related bills (keyword search e.g. 'short-term rental', 'vacation rental') across every state legislature in one client.
candidates.why_useful: Turns gap #12 (STR ordinance/registration trackers) into a pullable, nationwide bill-tracking method rather than a one-city hand-built database — could build a state-by-state STR-restriction bill count/status series as a regulatory-intensity index.
candidates.size_hint: API client only, no stored data

candidates.name: sh-patterson/legiscan-mcp
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP server wrapping the LegiScan API for bill search, full text, votes, legislator lookup, and change monitoring across all 50 states and Congress. Method only, no committed data.
candidates.why_useful: Same value as pylegiscan but agent-native (MCP) — could be pointed at STR/vacation-rental keyword bills for an ongoing regulatory-tracking feed.

candidates.name: BetaNYC/nyc-council-mcp
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP server for NYC Council legislative data pulled live via the Legistar API (bills, committee votes, hearing calendars). No stored dataset, but a working, current (updated July 2026) client scoped to exactly the council whose Local Law 18 (STR registration) most affects our NYC gap.
candidates.why_useful: Could pull the full NYC Council legislative history/amendments around Local Law 18 and any follow-on STR bills, useful context for interpreting the NYC Inside Airbnb dump gap (2023-06 to 2024-03) that gap #1 flags.

candidates.name: timmKal01/city-council-watch
candidates.what_it_holds: Apify actor that polls each city's Legistar instance for new ordinances/resolutions and upcoming council meetings, generic across any Legistar-hosted city council (many major US cities use Legistar).
candidates.why_useful: A generic, running scraper/method that could be filtered for STR-ordinance keywords across many US cities at once (LA, SF, Austin, Nashville, New Orleans, San Diego are all candidate Legistar cities in our Inside Airbnb panel), turning a one-off ordinance database into an always-on feed.

candidates.name: JenniferYao968/NLIHC
candidates.what_it_holds: Legislative-data extraction pipeline using the LegiScan API scoped to housing-policy bills (built with/for National Low Income Housing Coalition framing), not STR-specific but housing-regulation adjacent.
candidates.why_useful: Adjacent to gap #13 (long-term rental/housing crossover) and gap #12; a housing-bill extraction pipeline could be re-pointed at STR-specific keywords with modest effort.
candidates.size_hint: pipeline only, unclear if any extracted bill data is committed

candidates.name: Chalkbeat/legiscan-client
candidates.what_it_holds: Node.js client for the LegiScan API, built by a newsroom (Chalkbeat) for tracking legislation generically (education-focused newsroom use, but the client itself is generic).
candidates.why_useful: Another maintained, generic LegiScan client (JS ecosystem) that could pull STR-bill keyword searches; redundant with pylegiscan/legiscan-mcp above for a Python-first pipeline.

candidates.name: wbuchanan/legiscanR
candidates.what_it_holds: R interface to the LegiScan API, generic bill/vote/legislator lookup across US states and Congress.
candidates.why_useful: Same value class as the Python/Node LegiScan clients above; only useful if the team's pipeline is R-based.

candidates.name: akash250298/Airbnb_Regulation_Project
candidates.what_it_holds: Analysis notebook examining Paris Airbnb listing/pricing trends and how local regulation has shaped the market; uses existing (likely Inside Airbnb) Paris data, no new dataset committed.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal — an analysis of a market we already hold (Paris is in our 13-city panel) rather than new data; worth a one-line flag only in case its regulation-event timeline (French STR rule changes, dates) is usable as a ready-made event list.

candidates.size_hint: notebook only, no new data files
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Paris is already in our 13-city Inside Airbnb panel

notes: gh search repos returned nothing for 'short term rental regulation database', 'courtlistener airbnb', and a combined 'STR ordinance tracker OR airbnb litigation OR DAC7 platform reporting' query -- there is no dedicated GitHub-hosted STR-ordinance database repo, CourtListener/RECAP client scoped to Airbnb litigation, or EU-parliament open-data repo touching STR/Airbnb that surfaced under gh search's ranking. LegiScan/Legistar space is crowded with generic API clients (7+ found) but every one is generic, not STR-scoped -- true value would come from running one of these clients with STR/vacation-rental keyword filters, which is an acquisition-method finding, not a stored dataset. WebSearch quota was exhausted mid-task (session-wide budget hit by other concurrent agents) after 2 queries, so CourtListener/RECAP and EU Parliament open-data angles were not independently WebSearch-verified beyond the gh search null result -- worth a follow-up scout with fresh WebSearch budget specifically on 'CourtListener API Airbnb short-term rental litigation' and 'EU Parliament open data platform economy Directive 2024/1028' (the EU STR data-collection and sharing regulation), since neither produced gh hits but WebSearch might surface repos gh's search ranking missed. The single strongest find is js-fitz/STR-Monitor: a real committed dataset (historical pre-2023 Inside Airbnb Boston vintages + city registration + LTR crossover data) that hits three numbered gaps at once.
